lessons.title: 人人都有價碼
lessons.imageAlt: A thoughtful person stands beside a large price tag and coins, illustrating the proverb's cynical metaphor.
lessons.imageAltZh: 一個人站在大型價錢牌和硬幣旁，呈現這句諺語的悲觀比喻。
lessons.imageCaption: The imaginary price tag represents the cynical claim that enough money or benefit can buy a person's loyalty or principles.
lessons.imageCaptionZh: 想像中的價錢牌代表一種悲觀看法：足夠的金錢或利益可以收買一個人的忠誠或原則。

examples.en: The businessman believed that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 那名商人相信人人都有價碼。

meaning.en: This proverb expresses the cynical belief that every person can eventually be persuaded to act dishonestly, abandon a principle or betray somebody if the money or personal benefit offered is great enough.
meaning.zh: 這句諺語以悲觀甚至犬儒的方式表示：只要有人提出足夠多的金錢、利益或其他好處，任何人最終都可能被說服做出不誠實的行為、放棄原則或背叛他人。
naturalZh: 只要利益夠大，任何人都可能動搖
人的忠誠或原則可以被收買
沒有人完全不受金錢或利益誘惑
任何人都有可能為利益妥協
meaning.tendencyEn: Price is figurative: it means the money or benefit supposedly needed to buy a person's honesty, loyalty or principles. The saying is a cynical generalisation, not an established fact.
meaning.tendencyZh: price 在這裏是比喻用法，指據說要付出多少金錢或利益，才可以「買下」一個人的誠信、忠誠或原則。這句話是悲觀的概括，而不是已證實的事實。

modelExample.sourceEn: The businessman believed that anyone could be persuaded to betray their principles if enough money was offered.
modelExample.sourceZh: 那名商人認為，只要出價夠高，任何人都可能被說服背棄原則。
modelExample.answerEn: The businessman believed that every man has his price.
modelExample.answerZh: 那名商人相信人人都有價碼。
modelExample.compressedEn: Anybody may abandon their principles if enough money is offered.
modelExample.compressedZh: 只要出價夠高，任何人都可能放棄原則。

register.labelZh: 句法中性；語氣強烈悲觀及犬儒
register.summaryEn: The grammar is neutral, but the meaning is strongly cynical and distrustful. Saying it directly about a particular person may be insulting because it suggests that the person has no firm principles.
register.summaryZh: 這個表達的句法本身屬中性，但意思帶有強烈的悲觀、不信任及犬儒色彩。直接用來形容某一個人可能令人感到受冒犯，因為它暗示對方沒有堅定原則。
contextsZh: 有關誠信及忠誠的辯論

tones.en: The speaker presents human loyalty as something that money or personal benefit can buy.
tones.zh: 說話者把人的忠誠描述成可以被金錢或個人利益收買的東西。

tones.en: The speaker may report a character's pessimistic view without personally agreeing with it.
tones.zh: 說話者可以轉述某個人物的悲觀看法，而不表示自己認同。

tones.en: The proverb can be quoted in order to challenge the idea that everybody can be bought.
tones.zh: 說話者可以引用這句諺語，質疑「所有人都可以被收買」的想法。

sensitiveContextsEn: direct accusations about a particular person's honesty
serious allegations of bribery or corruption
situations where traditional gendered wording may distract or offend
sensitiveContextsZh: 直接質疑某一個人的誠信
嚴重的賄賂或貪污指控
傳統性別用語可能令人分心或不適的情況
register.sensitivityEn: The traditional words man and his once referred to people in general, but they are now gendered and may sound old-fashioned. Gender-neutral alternatives include everyone has a price and everyone can be bought; this exercise nevertheless practises the exact traditional proverb.
register.sensitivityZh: 傳統上，man 和 his 可以泛指所有人，但現代英語中這兩個字帶有性別色彩，也可能顯得較古老。較中性的說法包括 everyone has a price 和 everyone can be bought；本練習仍會練習指定的傳統諺語。
register.formalEn: Use the proverb only when its cynical attitude genuinely suits the context. A plain, evidence-based explanation is usually safer in highly formal or sensitive writing.
register.formalZh: 只有當這句諺語的悲觀語氣確實符合語境時才應使用。在高度正式或敏感的文字中，直接而有證據的說明通常更加穩妥。

fixedVariable.fixedEn: The five words remain fixed and must appear in this order.
fixedVariable.fixedZh: 這五個字及其排列次序不可改變。

capitalisation.en: Capitalise the first word when the proverb begins a sentence.
capitalisation.zh: 諺語放在句首時，第一個字母使用大寫。

capitalisation.example: He believes that every man has his price.
capitalisation.en: Use lower case when the proverb sits inside a longer sentence.
capitalisation.zh: 諺語放在較長句子中時，通常使用小寫。

fixedVariable.variableEn: The proverb itself normally remains unchanged. The reporting frame, speaker position, tense and certainty around it may vary.
fixedVariable.variableZh: 諺語本身通常保持不變；可以改變的是外圍的轉述框架、說話者立場、時態及確定程度。
variableItemsEn: the tense of the reporting verb

forms.example: He believes that every man has his price.
He believed that every man has his price.
forms.exampleZh: 他當時相信人人都有價碼。

forms.example: He has always believed that every man has his price.
forms.exampleZh: 他一直相信人人都有價碼。

forms.example: He will argue that every man has his price.
forms.exampleZh: 他將會主張人人都有價碼。

forms.example: Does Marcus really believe that every man has his price?
forms.exampleZh: Marcus 真的相信人人都有價碼嗎？

forms.example: “Every man has his price,” the dealer said.
forms.exampleZh: 那名商人說：「人人都有價碼。」

forms.example: She rejects the idea that every man has his price.
forms.exampleZh: 她反駁「人人都有價碼」這個想法。

specificForms.descriptionEn: Use the proverb as a complete statement when the cynical belief is already clear.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 當這種悲觀信念已經清楚時，可以把諺語當作完整陳述。

examples.en: Every man has his price.
examples.zh: 人人都有價碼。

specificForms.formula: Subject + believe / think / say / claim + that + every man has his price.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Use a reporting verb to attribute the cynical belief to another person or character.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 使用轉述動詞，把這種悲觀看法歸於另一個人或角色。

examples.en: The businessman believed that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 那名商人相信人人都有價碼。

notes.en: Has may remain in the present simple after a past reporting verb because the proverb states a general belief.
notes.zh: 即使轉述動詞使用過去式，諺語中的 has 仍可保留現在式，因為它表達一般信念。

specificForms.titleEn: Describing the Belief as an Idea
specificForms.formula: Subject + present / express / hold + the belief that + every man has his price.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Name the proverb as a belief rather than presenting it as fact.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 把諺語明確稱為一種信念，而不是把它說成事實。

examples.en: The film presents the belief that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 這齣電影提出「人人都有價碼」這個信念。

specificForms.formula: Subject + question / challenge / reject + the idea that + every man has his price.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Use this frame when the source questions or rejects the proverb.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 原句質疑或反駁這句諺語時，使用這個框架。

examples.en: Her refusal challenges the idea that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 她的拒絕質疑了「人人都有價碼」這個想法。

specificForms.formula: Does + subject + believe that + every man has his price?
specificForms.descriptionEn: Ask whether somebody genuinely accepts the cynical belief.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 詢問某人是否真的認同這種悲觀看法。

examples.en: Does Marcus really believe that every man has his price?
examples.zh: Marcus 真的相信人人都有價碼嗎？

specificForms.formula: “Every man has his price,” + subject + said.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Quote the proverb directly and identify the speaker.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 直接引用整句諺語，並指出說話者。

examples.en: “Every man has his price,” the dealer said.
examples.zh: 那名商人說：「人人都有價碼。」

specificForms.formula: Although / Because / If + subject + believes that every man has his price, ...
specificForms.descriptionEn: Connect the reported belief to contrasting evidence, a reason or a condition.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 把被轉述的信念連接到相反證據、原因或條件。

examples.en: Although the director believes that every man has his price, the worker refuses every offer.
examples.zh: 雖然主管相信人人都有價碼，但員工拒絕了所有提議。

benefits.en: The proverb compresses the idea that anybody may abandon their principles if enough money is offered.
benefits.zh: 這句諺語把「只要金額足夠，任何人最終都可能放棄原則」這個較長概念濃縮成容易記憶的表達。

examples.en: He believes that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 他相信人人都有價碼。

benefits.en: The expression reveals a pessimistic and distrustful view of human honesty.
benefits.zh: 這個表達顯示說話者對人的誠信抱有悲觀和不信任的態度。

benefits.en: It is useful when analysing a villain or dishonest character who believes that loyalty and principles can be bought.
benefits.zh: 分析反派、不誠實商人或其他相信忠誠和原則可以被收買的角色時，這句話十分有用。

benefits.titleEn: It Can Be Accepted, Questioned or Rejected
benefits.en: Different grammatical frames let the speaker report, question or reject the belief.
benefits.zh: 不同的句法框架讓學生可以轉述、質疑或反駁這個信念。

examples.en: Do you believe that every man has his price?
examples.zh: 你相信人人都有價碼嗎？

examples.en: She rejects the idea that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 她反駁「人人都有價碼」這個想法。

benefits.en: Students may encounter the proverb in films, crime stories, political commentary and discussions about corruption or loyalty.
benefits.zh: 學生可能會在電影、犯罪故事、政治評論，以及有關貪污或忠誠的討論中遇到這句諺語。

origin.statusEn: Early Record Well Documented; Exact Origin Unknown
origin.statusZh: 早期記錄有較充分證據；確切起源不明

history.en: One early documented form appeared in 1734 in connection with a speech by William Wyndham. It was described as an old maxim, suggesting that the saying was already known. The proverb is often attributed to Robert Walpole, but a later account records his narrower comment, “All those men have their price,” about a particular group of politicians; the broader proverb should not be presented as his proven invention.
history.zh: 其中一個較早而有記錄的版本在 1734 年出現，與 William Wyndham 的一篇演說有關。講者稱它為一句「古老格言」，顯示當時很可能已經流傳。這句諺語經常被歸於 Robert Walpole，但較後期記錄所載的是他針對一群特定政治人物所說的「那些人都有價碼」；因此不應把較廣泛的諺語說成肯定由他創造。

history.en: The ordinary word price refers to the money required to buy something. The proverb extends that idea metaphorically to human behaviour: money or personal advantage is imagined as buying cooperation, silence or betrayal.
history.zh: price 一般指購買物件所需的金額。這句諺語把概念比喻性地延伸至人的行為：金錢或個人利益被想像成可以購買一個人的合作、沉默或背叛。

history.en: Today, the expression remains a deliberately cynical claim that no person's honesty or loyalty is completely beyond temptation. It may also be quoted in order to question or reject that belief.
history.zh: 今天，這個表達仍然是一種刻意悲觀的說法，聲稱沒有人的誠信或忠誠能完全不受誘惑；說話者也可以引用它來質疑或反駁這種看法。

origin.memoryEn: A price tag suggests that something can be bought. The proverb cynically places an imaginary price tag on a person's principles.
origin.memoryZh: 價錢牌代表某件東西可以被購買。這句諺語悲觀地把一個想像中的價錢牌掛在人的原則之上。

rules.titleEn: Reproduce the Exact Proverb
rules.titleZh: 準確重現整句諺語
rules.en: Every answer must contain the exact five-word proverb in the correct order.
rules.zh: 每個答案都必須準確包含五個字的目標諺語，不可更換或調動任何部分。

examples.en: every man has his price
examples.zh: 人人都有價碼

rules.titleEn: Price Is Figurative
rules.titleZh: price 是比喻意思
rules.en: The expression concerns supposedly buying a person's honesty, loyalty or principles, not the selling price of a product.
rules.zh: 這個表達指據說可以收買一個人的誠信、忠誠或原則，而不是貨品的售價。

examples.en: The criminal believes that every man has his price.
examples.zh: 那名罪犯相信人人都有價碼。

rules.titleEn: Use It for Bribery or Moral Compromise
rules.titleZh: 用於賄賂或道德妥協
rules.en: Use it when money or another benefit may cause dishonesty, betrayal, disclosure of a secret, disregard of a rule or abandonment of a moral principle.
rules.zh: 金錢或利益可能令人不誠實、背叛他人、洩露秘密、忽視規則或放棄道德原則時，才適合使用。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use It for Normal Payment
rules.titleZh: 不可用於正常報酬
rules.en: Receiving a salary, charging a fair price or accepting ordinary payment does not normally mean that somebody has been bought.
rules.zh: 收取薪金、訂立合理價錢或接受正常報酬，通常不代表某人被收買。

examples.en: The chef agreed to work for a monthly salary.
examples.zh: 廚師同意按月薪工作。

rules.titleEn: Preserve the Speaker's Position
rules.titleZh: 保留說話者的立場
rules.en: Do not turn a source that questions, reports or rejects the proverb into a statement of fact.
rules.zh: 不可把質疑、轉述或反駁這句諺語的原句，改成確定事實。

examples.en: The film asks whether every man has his price.
examples.zh: 電影提出疑問：是否人人都有價碼。

rules.titleEn: Preserve Certainty
rules.titleZh: 保留確定程度
rules.en: Words such as seems, suggests, may and believes show that the statement is an opinion rather than a proven fact.
rules.zh: seems、suggests、may 和 believes 等字詞表示這只是一個觀點，而不是已證實的事實。

rules.titleEn: Use the Gendered Traditional Form Carefully
rules.titleZh: 小心使用傳統性別用語
rules.en: The traditional proverb uses man and his but intends to include people of any gender. A gender-neutral alternative may be more appropriate outside this exact-form exercise.
rules.zh: 傳統諺語使用 man 和 his，但原意泛指任何性別的人。在本練習以外，較中性的說法有時會更合適。

rules.titleEn: The Proverb Does Not Approve of Bribery
rules.titleZh: 這句諺語並不表示贊成賄賂
rules.en: A speaker may quote the proverb in order to criticise, question or reject its cynical belief.
rules.zh: 說話者可以引用這句諺語來批評、質疑或反駁其中的犬儒看法。

instructions.en: Rewrite or respond to each item using every man has his price. Type the whole sentence; the first word of the model answer is provided.
instructions.zh: 使用 every man has his price 改寫句子或完成回應。請輸入完整句子；每題已提供參考答案的第一個字。

lessons.title: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩
lessons.titleZh: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩
lessons.imageAlt: A hand pulls back from a warning snake after an earlier bite, illustrating greater caution after a bad experience.
lessons.imageAltZh: 一隻手曾經被咬後，對警戒中的蛇退縮，呈現受過一次傷害後更加謹慎的意思。
lessons.imageCaption: The earlier bite represents a bad experience; pulling back represents the caution that follows.
lessons.imageCaptionZh: 先前的咬傷代表不愉快經歷；其後退縮代表由此產生的謹慎。

examples.en: Once bitten, twice shy: Rachel now asks for a written agreement before paying any new company.
examples.zh: 吃過一次虧，Rachel 現在會在付款給任何新公司前，先要求一份書面協議。

meaning.en: After somebody has been hurt, disappointed, deceived or otherwise affected by an unpleasant experience, they become more cautious or reluctant when facing the same or a similar situation again.
meaning.zh: 某人曾經受傷、失望、受騙或經歷不愉快的事情後，再遇到相同或類似情況時，便會變得更加小心、猶豫或不願再次冒險。
naturalZh: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩
吃過一次虧，便加倍小心
有了上次的教訓，今次不敢大意
曾經受過傷，因此不敢輕易再試
因過往的不愉快經歷而變得謹慎
前車可鑑，不敢重蹈覆轍
meaning.tendencyEn: The bite is normally figurative, and shy means cautious or reluctant rather than socially quiet. A suitable context links an earlier bad experience to later caution in a related situation.
meaning.tendencyZh: bite 通常屬比喻用法；shy 表示謹慎或不願再次冒險，而不是社交上的害羞。合適語境會把先前的不愉快經歷與其後相關情況中的謹慎連繫起來。

modelExample.sourceEn: The last company charged Rachel for work it never completed. She now asks for a written agreement before paying any new company.
modelExample.sourceZh: 上一間公司向 Rachel 收取了沒有完成的工作費用。她現在會在付款給任何新公司前，先要求一份書面協議。
modelExample.answerEn: Once bitten, twice shy: Rachel now asks for a written agreement before paying any new company.
modelExample.answerZh: 吃過一次虧，Rachel 現在會在付款給任何新公司前，先要求一份書面協議。
preservedEn: present caution caused by past experience
preservedZh: 上一間公司未完成工作
過往經歷造成目前的謹慎
modelExample.compressedEn: A previous bad experience has made Rachel more cautious in a similar situation.
modelExample.compressedZh: 先前的不愉快經歷令 Rachel 在類似情況中變得更加謹慎。

register.summaryEn: The proverb is natural in everyday communication and can communicate sensible caution, fear, hesitation, distrust, regret, sympathy or mild humour, depending on context.
register.summaryZh: 這句諺語自然地用於日常溝通，並可按語境帶出理性謹慎、恐懼、猶豫、不信任、後悔、同情或輕微幽默。
contextsEn: comments about trust, risk and past mistakes
contextsZh: 有關信任、風險及過往錯誤的評論

tones.en: The speaker presents later checks or safeguards as an understandable lesson from experience.
tones.zh: 說話者把其後的核對或保障措施，描述成從經驗汲取的合理教訓。

tones.en: The proverb can explain why trust has weakened or why somebody is reluctant to try again.
tones.zh: 這句諺語可以解釋信任為甚麼減弱，或某人為甚麼不願再次嘗試。

tones.en: In an ordinary, low-stakes situation, it may gently acknowledge a person's increased caution.
tones.zh: 在一般而風險不高的情況中，它可以溫和地表示理解某人變得更加小心。

sensitiveContextsEn: situations requiring sustained empathy rather than a short proverb
sensitiveContextsZh: 需要持續同理而不適合只用一句諺語回應的情況
register.sensitivityEn: Using a short proverb in response to severe trauma, abuse or serious loss may sound dismissive or lacking in sympathy.
register.sensitivityZh: 如果別人正在談論嚴重創傷、虐待或重大損失，只以一句簡短諺語回應，可能令人覺得說話者輕視對方的感受或缺乏同理心。
register.formalEn: The proverb suits general communication. In highly formal analysis, explain the earlier experience and later caution directly if the connection may not be obvious.
register.formalZh: 這句諺語適合一般溝通。在高度正式的分析中，如果前因後果未必清楚，應直接說明先前經歷與其後謹慎之間的關係。

fixedVariable.fixedEn: All four words remain fixed, and the comma after bitten should normally be retained.
fixedVariable.fixedZh: 四個字全部屬於固定部分；bitten 後面的逗號通常必須保留。

capitalisation.en: Capitalise Once when the proverb begins a sentence.
capitalisation.zh: 諺語放在句首時，Once 的第一個字母使用大寫。

capitalisation.labelEn: At the end of a sentence
capitalisation.example: She now checks every detail—once bitten, twice shy.
capitalisation.en: Lower case is natural after a dash inside a longer sentence.
capitalisation.zh: 在較長句子中放在破折號後時，通常使用小寫。

fixedVariable.variableEn: The proverb does not normally change. What changes is the grammatical frame around it and the explanation of the earlier experience or later caution.
fixedVariable.variableZh: 目標諺語本身通常不會改變；可以改變的是前後的句法框架，以及先前經歷或其後謹慎的說明。
variableItemsEn: a concluding comment after a dash

forms.exampleZh: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩。

forms.example: Once bitten, twice shy: I now check every detail.
forms.exampleZh: 吃過一次虧，我現在會核對每項細節。

forms.example: As the saying goes, once bitten, twice shy.
forms.exampleZh: 正所謂一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩。

forms.example: It was a case of once bitten, twice shy.
forms.exampleZh: 這正是一朝被蛇咬、十年怕草繩。
Priya 解釋道：「一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩。」

forms.example: He now pays only after delivery—once bitten, twice shy.
forms.exampleZh: 他現在只會在收貨後付款；有了上次教訓，自然更加小心。

specificForms.descriptionEn: Use the proverb alone only when the previous bad experience is already clear from the conversation.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 只有當對話中已清楚交代先前的不愉快經歷時，才適合單獨使用。

examples.en: Once bitten, twice shy.
examples.zh: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩。

specificForms.formula: Once bitten, twice shy: + complete clause.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Use a colon when the following clause explains how the person has become more cautious.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 後面的句子解釋某人現在如何變得更加謹慎時，可以使用冒號。

examples.en: Once bitten, twice shy: I now read every agreement carefully.
examples.zh: 吃過一次虧，我現在會仔細閱讀每份協議。

specificForms.formula: As the saying goes, once bitten, twice shy.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Introduce the expression explicitly as a well-known saying.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 明確把這個表達作為廣為人知的諺語引入。

examples.en: As the saying goes, once bitten, twice shy. I will check the details more carefully this time.
examples.zh: 正所謂一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩。今次我會更加仔細核對資料。

specificForms.formula: It is / was a case of once bitten, twice shy.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Describe a particular person's situation as an instance of the proverb.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 把某人的具體情況描述成這句諺語的一個例子。

examples.en: For Aaron, it was a case of once bitten, twice shy: he had lost money before and would not take the same risk again.
examples.zh: 對 Aaron 而言，這正是一朝被蛇咬、十年怕草繩：他以前曾損失金錢，所以不願再冒同樣風險。

specificForms.formula: Complete clause + dash + once bitten, twice shy.
specificForms.descriptionEn: The dash separates the situation from the speaker's concluding comment.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 破折號把具體情況與說話者的總結分開。

examples.en: She now asks for everything in writing—once bitten, twice shy.
examples.zh: 她現在會要求所有事情以書面確認；畢竟吃過一次虧，自然會更加小心。

specificForms.formula: “Once bitten, twice shy,” + speaker + reporting verb.
specificForms.descriptionEn: Quote the proverb directly and identify the speaker with a reporting clause.
specificForms.descriptionZh: 直接引用整句諺語，再以轉述小句指出說話者。

examples.en: “Once bitten, twice shy,” Clara explained.
examples.zh: Clara 解釋道：「一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩。」

notes.en: In standard British dialogue punctuation, the comma appears inside the closing quotation mark when a reporting clause follows.
notes.zh: 在標準英式對話標點中，如果引號後接報告句，逗號會放在結束引號之內。

benefits.titleEn: It Connects Past Experience with Present Behaviour
benefits.titleZh: 把過往經歷與目前行為連繫起來
benefits.en: The proverb clearly links an earlier unpleasant experience with present caution.
benefits.zh: 這個諺語把過往的不愉快經歷與目前的謹慎行為清楚連繫起來。

examples.en: She checks every seller carefully now—once bitten, twice shy.
examples.zh: 她現在會仔細查核每名賣家；吃過一次虧，自然更加小心。

benefits.en: It expresses in one short saying that a bad experience has made somebody worried and more careful.
benefits.zh: 一句簡短諺語便可表達「曾經吃虧，所以現在更加謹慎」這個完整意思。

examples.en: Once bitten, twice shy.
examples.zh: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩。

benefits.titleEn: It Explains Reluctance Without Calling It Irrational
benefits.titleZh: 解釋猶豫，而不一定批評對方不理性
benefits.en: The expression often presents caution as an understandable result of experience.
benefits.zh: 這個表達通常把謹慎描述為過往經驗所造成的合理反應，而不一定是在批評對方過分膽小。

benefits.titleEn: It Can Describe Different Levels of Caution
benefits.titleZh: 可以表達不同程度的謹慎
benefits.en: The person may stop, delay, check more carefully, ask for proof, try on a smaller scale or proceed only under conditions.
benefits.zh: 當事人可以完全停止、延遲決定、更加仔細檢查、要求證明、先作小規模嘗試，或只在符合條件時再次參與。

benefits.titleEn: It Is Useful as a Conversational Response
benefits.titleZh: 適合作為自然的對話回應
benefits.en: When both speakers know the background, the proverb can form a short but meaningful reply.
benefits.zh: 當雙方已知道事情背景時，這句諺語可以構成簡短而有意義的回應。

examples.en: Once bitten, twice shy.
examples.zh: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩。

benefits.titleEn: It Helps Learners Understand Authentic English
benefits.titleZh: 幫助學生理解真實英語
benefits.en: The saying commonly appears when people discuss trust, risk, disappointment and lessons learned from experience.
benefits.zh: 人們談論信任、風險、失望或從經驗中汲取教訓時，經常會使用這句諺語。

origin.statusZh: 逐漸形成；確切來源不明

history.en: The general lesson that a person becomes cautious after being harmed is older than the modern wording, but this does not prove that one ancient story directly created the English proverb. A close early form, “once bit twice shy,” appears in Rachel Hunter's 1806 novel Lady Maclairn, the Victim of Villany.
history.zh: 「受過傷害後便會變得謹慎」這個道理遠早於現代英文句式，但不能證明某一個古代故事直接創造了這句諺語。一個非常接近的早期形式 once bit twice shy 出現在 Rachel Hunter 1806 年的小說 Lady Maclairn, the Victim of Villany 中。

history.en: The early form used bit rather than bitten. The modern wording once bitten, twice shy was recorded in G. F. Northall's 1894 collection Folk-Phrases of Four Counties. Historical references also distinguish the British once bitten form from the American once burned variant.
history.zh: 較早期形式使用 bit，而不是 bitten。現代形式 once bitten, twice shy 收錄於 G. F. Northall 在 1894 年出版的 Folk-Phrases of Four Counties。歷史資料亦把英式 once bitten 與美式 once burned 變體區分開來。

history.en: Today, the proverb means that a previous failure, injury or disappointment has made somebody more cautious about trying something similar again.
history.zh: 今天，這句諺語表示某人因先前的失敗、傷害或失望，在再次面對類似事情時變得更加小心。

origin.memoryEn: The first bite causes the later shyness: one bad experience produces greater caution next time.
origin.memoryZh: 第一次「被咬」造成其後的「退縮」：一次不愉快的經歷，令人下一次更加謹慎。

rules.titleEn: Keep Every Word Fixed
rules.titleZh: 所有字詞必須保持不變
rules.en: Use the exact four-word expression; a similar phrase such as once hurt, twice shy is not the target.
rules.zh: 必須使用四個字的完整目標表達；once hurt, twice shy 即使意思相近，也不是本練習指定的諺語。

examples.en: once bitten, twice shy
examples.zh: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩

rules.titleEn: Retain the Comma
rules.titleZh: 保留逗號
rules.en: The comma reflects the parallel relationship between the two parts and should normally be retained.
rules.zh: 逗號反映前後兩部分的平行及因果關係，通常必須保留。

examples.en: Once bitten, twice shy.
examples.zh: 一朝被蛇咬，十年怕草繩。

rules.titleEn: Bitten Is Usually Figurative
rules.titleZh: bitten 通常屬於比喻意思
rules.en: The speaker need not have been physically bitten. Bitten can represent deception, financial loss, disappointment, poor service, a costly mistake or another unpleasant result.
rules.zh: 說話者不需要真的曾經被動物咬傷。bitten 可以比喻受騙、損失金錢、失望、差劣服務、代價高昂的錯誤或其他不愉快後果。

rules.titleEn: Shy Does Not Mean Socially Quiet
rules.titleZh: shy 並非指社交上的害羞
rules.en: Here, shy means cautious, nervous or unwilling to take the same risk again.
rules.zh: 在這句諺語中，shy 表示謹慎、擔心或不願再次冒相同風險。

rules.titleEn: Two Time Stages Are Required
rules.titleZh: 必須包含兩個時間階段
rules.en: A suitable context contains an earlier unpleasant experience and later caution in a similar situation.
rules.zh: 合適語境包括較早前的不愉快經歷，以及其後面對類似情況時所表現的謹慎。

examples.en: Once bitten, twice shy: I now check every seller carefully.
examples.zh: 吃過一次虧，我現在會仔細查核每名賣家。

rules.titleEn: The Later Situation Must Be Related
rules.titleZh: 後來的情況必須與原先經歷有關
rules.en: The later precaution must respond to the same or a genuinely similar risk.
rules.zh: 其後採取的預防措施，必須回應相同或真正相近的風險。

rules.titleEn: It Does Not Always Mean Complete Refusal
rules.titleZh: 不一定表示完全拒絕
rules.en: It may mean refusing, waiting, asking questions, checking details, making a smaller commitment, requiring protection or proceeding under conditions.
rules.zh: 它可以表示拒絕、等待、提問、核對細節、先作較小承諾、要求保障，或只在特定條件下行動。

rules.titleEn: Preserve Certainty and Modality
rules.titleZh: 保留確定程度及情態意思
rules.en: Do not turn may be more careful into a definite and permanent refusal.
rules.zh: 不可把「可能會更加小心」改成確定而永久的拒絕。

examples.en: He may be more careful next time—once bitten, twice shy.
examples.zh: 他下次可能會更加小心；畢竟吃過一次虧。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Use It Without a Bad First Experience
rules.titleZh: 沒有先前的不愉快經歷時，不應使用
rules.en: Ordinary careful research, without an earlier hurt, deception or disappointment, does not establish the proverb's meaning.
rules.zh: 如果沒有先前的受傷、受騙或失望，只是一般仔細研究，便未能構成這句諺語的意思。

rules.titleEn: Do Not Repeat the Whole Meaning
rules.titleZh: 不要在使用諺語後完整重複其意思
rules.en: Let the proverb compress the connection between the past experience and present caution; add a concrete current action instead of repeating the definition.
rules.zh: 讓諺語濃縮「過往經歷導致現在謹慎」的意思；其後應加入具體行動，而不是重複定義。

examples.en: Once bitten, twice shy: he now checks every agreement before signing it.
examples.zh: 吃過一次虧，他現在會在簽署前仔細檢查每份協議。

rules.titleEn: Related Variants Are Not the Target
rules.titleZh: 相關變體不是本練習目標
rules.en: Once bit, twice shy, once burned, twice shy and a burnt child dreads the fire may occur in authentic English, but this exercise requires the exact target proverb.
rules.zh: once bit, twice shy、once burned, twice shy 和 a burnt child dreads the fire 等相關形式可以出現在真實英語中，但本練習必須使用指定諺語。

examples.en: once bitten, twice shy
examples.zh: 本練習的指定形式

rules.titleEn: Use It Sensitively
rules.titleZh: 注意使用時的敏感程度
rules.en: The saying suits ordinary disappointments, mistakes and risks. In response to severe trauma, abuse or serious loss, it may sound dismissive or unsympathetic.
rules.zh: 這句諺語適合一般失望、錯誤和風險；回應嚴重創傷、虐待或重大損失時，可能令人覺得輕視對方或缺乏同理心。

instructions.en: Rewrite or respond to each item using once bitten, twice shy. Type the whole sentence; the first word of the model answer is provided.
instructions.zh: 使用 once bitten, twice shy 改寫句子或完成回應。請輸入完整句子；每題已提供參考答案的第一個字。
